_about: Hand-checked data for the list of LLM solutions (Lasry, 25-26 Sept 2026). Sections: ct = key recovered from ciphertext only; extpt = key rebuilt from a plaintext found outside the collection (another archive, a print, a website, an unrelated record); extkey = an existing key found outside the collection and matched; borderline = key or plaintext found elsewhere in the same collection (different volume or fonds), left for Lasry to decide. Same-file siblings are not listed. primary = the original; secondary = where the target was found; found = where the key or plaintext came from. *_links are [label, url]; DECODE R-numbers are linked automatically. part = the outcome.parts label of a split target. Method, extent and the unpublished-prior note come from each profile.json.

items.title: Sienese envoys and others to the government of Siena
items.primary: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308, fasc. 2 "Lettere in cifra"
items.secondary: DECODE R4790-R4814 (no status); the archive's 1952 inventory calls the letters 'solo parzialmente decifrate'
items.summary: Keys recovered from the ciphertext alone for three letters (nos. 25, 18, 14) and from an alphabet fragment for a fourth; none of the 43 keys filed with the letters fits. No. 25 reads 96.2%, no. 18 (Latin treaty articles with the Emperor) 87.1%. Several other letters in the file remain open.

items.title: Matheo de Segura to the Constable of Castile
items.primary: BnF, espagnol 336 no. 99, ff. 196r-198r
items.secondary: Tomokiyo, cryptiana (spanish3.htm, unsolved.htm): the last es. 336 item listed as undeciphered
items.summary: Two short passages in a homophonic cipher; the key was rebuilt by annealing and resegmenting the image. 119 of 125 cipher tokens read (95.2%). The passages concern predictions of the world ending or the king dying by September.

items.title: Giovan Gioacchino da Passano (attributed), London, to Francis I
items.primary: BnF, Clairambault 331, ff. 156-157
items.summary: An account of Wolsey's wealth: cash, credits, revenues, jewels and plate, Winchester, St Albans and York. A dotted re-transcription made the break possible. 386 of 402 signs read coherently (96.0%).

items.title: Mémoire en chiffre to the connétable de Montmorency
items.primary: BnF, français 3157 no. 67, ff. 152r-156v
items.secondary: BnF catalogue (Gallica harvest); no DECODE record
items.summary: Ten pages in a cursive pseudo-script: a homophonic substitution with two-stroke units and four word codes, broken from the images alone. It reports on the Protestant rising in the Agenais a week after François II's death. 98.9% of 1,715 cipher words read.

items.title: "L'Estat du Roy de Navarre et de son party en France"
items.primary: British Library, Harley MS 1582, ff. 263-264
items.summary: A French memoir on Navarre's party in a homophonic alphabet of about 50 graphic signs. The letter m is written as a group of dots, which earlier passes took for punctuation. 95.1% read.

items.title: Ferenc Wesselényi, Palatine of Hungary, to Leopold I
items.primary: MNL OL E 199 (Wesselényi family archive), 8. pallium 1. 01
items.summary: A reversed-alphabet cipher with vowel homophones in a Latin draft, broken by annealing and then corrected by hand. A general is to take His Majesty's garrison by force if need be. 98.8% of cipher tokens read; two codes are open.

items.title: Sir Simonds D'Ewes, cipher log of his son's convulsion fits
items.primary: British Library, Harley MS 286, f. 61
items.secondary: DECODE R7759 ("unknown sender to unknown recipient, 1635")
items.summary: D'Ewes's private alphabet over Latin, rebuilt from cribs (convulsio, plena luna); the weekdays and moon phases check out against his Autobiography. 96.5% of 287 words read.

items.title: Unknown writer to Hesse-Kassel
items.primary: Hessisches Staatsarchiv Marburg, HStAM 4 d Nr. 1218, no. 49
items.summary: A digit-and-sign letter substitution. None of the volume's ~120 key sheets fits; the key was annealed on German of the period and confirmed by the contemporary gloss on lines 1-4. About 97% read.

items.title: Ferdinand of Bavaria, Elector of Cologne, to Duke Maximilian I of Bavaria
items.primary: Bayerisches Hauptstaatsarchiv, Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591, ff. 281-286
items.secondary: DECODE R9426 (non-decrypted, no author or recipient)
items.summary: Ten pages in a homophonic substitution on two-digit figures with a nomenclator, broken by annealing 2,482 letters; the key reads the sibling R9425 unchanged. The letter covers quartering and troops six weeks after Frederick V's coronation. 95.8% read.

items.title: Swatow telegram to Sun Yat-sen
items.primary: JACAR (Japan Center for Asian Historical Records) B03050738800
items.secondary: Tomokiyo, cryptiana list and blog (12 Dec 2021), unsolved since 2021
items.summary: Standard Chinese telegraph code passed through a systematic code condenser, recovered by brute force. 41 of about 44 characters read.

items.title: Sun Yat-sen's intercepted telegrams
items.primary: JACAR, 特定人ノ発受郵便物取調 (Ministry of Communications intercepts)
items.summary: About 60 condenser telegrams read under seven keys of the Swatow family, plus the Hankow +111 digit code, including Chen Qimei's assassination as reported to Tokyo. Sun's six-vowel 文密 code is still open.

items.title: Warsaw letter to the Bishop of Olmütz (?)
items.primary: ÖStA HHStA, Staatskanzlei Interiora, Chiffrenschlüssel Kt. 14 Fasc. 20 f. 176
items.secondary: DECODE R1408 (non-decrypted); transcription by Tomokiyo, cryptiana (variable2.htm, unsolved.htm)
items.summary: A homophonic substitution whose alphabet is in plain order, with syllables, nulls and thirteen word codes, recovered by annealing. The writer presses for a canonry of Olmütz for a son of the Queen of Poland. Read in full; the word codes are glossed from context.

items.title: Henry of Navarre to Ségur
items.primary: BnF, 500 de Colbert 401, ff. 233, 239, 288v
items.secondary: Tomokiyo, cryptiana unsolved list (as letters of Henry III)
items.summary: Three figure-cipher letters to the envoy raising a German army. The key, an alphabetical syllabary, was rebuilt by a structured annealer and checked on matched controls. The letters cover Duke Casimir, Clervant's reiters and the road through the Vivarais.

items.title: Cardinal Soglia to nuncio Viale Prelà at Innsbruck
items.primary: L'Italia del Popolo no. 40 (Milan, 30 June 1848), Roman broadsheet reprint
items.summary: A 64-cell two-digit table with homophones and syllables, 5 as word separator, and an alphabetical one-part code. It is a counter-order: stay with the Emperor and suspend the request for passports. Ten code words read from context; 11 code groups open.

items.title: Gottfried van Swieten to Count Cobenzl
items.primary: Archives générales du Royaume, Brussels, Secrétairerie d'État et de Guerre 1236
items.summary: The 1759 table (groups 100-442) was rebuilt ciphertext-only by monotone annealing against French, then corrected by hand. The despatches cover the Gueldre convention and Soubise's army. 96% of 553 groups read.

items.title: Johann Heinrich Kauderbach (The Hague) to Brühl / Friedrich August II
items.primary: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague, Prins Willem V inv. 201
items.secondary: DECODE R1043, R1044, R1954, R1958, R1959, R2078-R2082 ("never solved" by the Hague cabinet)
items.summary: Unseparated figures in which 5 and 8 are nulls; one key serves all ten despatches. It was found by one-to-one annealing onto the vocabulary of his 1761 key. All ten despatches read at 65-97%, covering the Dutch augmentation debate and the Treaty of Versailles.

items.title: Potocka and Mniszech to Jakub Dunin
items.primary: Archiwum Narodowe w Krakowie, Archiwum Sanguszków
items.summary: Potocka's alphabet was broken from a Polish postscript and carried over to eight French letters; 97.3% of Potocka tokens valued. Mniszech's letter is still unread.

items.title: Four cipher letters to Gianfrancesco Gonzaga, lord of Mantua
items.primary: Archivio di Stato di Mantova, Archivio Gonzaga
items.secondary: DECODE R1854 (partially decrypted; catalogued as one letter)
items.summary: Two keys rebuilt ciphertext-only: Rome, 9 Aug 1428 (96.6%) and Cattanei, Feb 1430 (96.7%). A third letter was re-deciphered from its interlinear gloss. Pandolfo Malatesta's own runs remain open. 91.5% of all signs read.

items.title: Guido Rangone (Venice) to Anne de Montmorency
items.primary: BnF, français 3070 f. 81 no. 40 and français 3082 f. 42 no. 19
items.secondary: DECODE R4249; Tomokiyo, cryptiana (francis.htm) lists both as undeciphered
items.summary: A homophonic substitution of about 50 signs for Italian, broken by annealing. Both passages concern Cesare Fregoso. 87.9% of signs read; four short runs are too short to resolve.

items.title: Thomas Edmondes (at Henri IV's court) to Lord Treasurer Burghley
items.primary: British Library, Stowe MS 166, ff. 50-61, 109-112
items.secondary: DECODE R7770-R7775 ("Lord Threr? to unknown recipient")
items.summary: Six letters from the King's camp with lines in invented signs: a simple substitution of English with homophones and person signs, broken from the clear context. Everything reads except four lines on f. 59.

items.title: Claude de La Guiche, bishop of Mirepoix (Rome), to Montmorency
items.primary: BnF, français 3138 no. 22, f. 60v
items.summary: A 406-sign passage in 22 invented signs, broken by permutation annealing. It covers the Count of Santa Fiora, 'mal satisfaict' and ready to serve the king on conditions. Seure's Lisbon letters in the same file are left open.

items.title: An Orange prince to an officer of the Dutch émigré troops
items.primary: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague, Prins Willem V inv. 339
items.summary: Vertical digit pairs from a 6x6 square, recovered by quadgram annealing on the Dutch postscript; the square then read the French page unchanged. The letter concerns General Dundas, pay and embarkation. 94% of cipher tokens read; about thirty word signs open.

items.title: Lope de Soria to Charles V: the key-A letters
items.primary: Real Academia de la Historia, Madrid, Colección Salazar y Castro A-28 (9/28)
items.summary: Split entry. Soria used two ciphers in 1523. Key A (the June letter in three copies and the body of the July letter) had no key and no crib; it was broken by simulated annealing on a Castilian model of the 1520s and read nearly throughout: the Venetian league bought with Milanese money, the French king's expected descent on Italy. The later key-B letters were read from a key rebuilt from an external decipherment (R9844) and are not counted here.

items.title: A Bavarian agent to the Dukes of Bavaria: the Pressburg talks
items.primary: Bayerisches Hauptstaatsarchiv, Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591, f. 263
items.summary: Split entry. 3,150 signs in a homophonic substitution, broken by constrained annealing against German of 1472-1609 on the first run; a faint gloss on the first lines agrees word for word. It reports the Pressburg negotiations between Ferdinand and John Zápolya, a Turkish embassy and Alvise Gritti. Running German with local errors; person codes open. The rest of this key volume was read from contemporary glosses and is not counted here.

items.title: Adrian of Utrecht, the Admiral and the Constable of Castile to Charles V
items.primary: Archivo General de Simancas, Estado leg. 8 no. 150
items.found: Gredilla's 19th-century decipherment printed by Danvila, Memorial Histórico Español 38 (1899), pp. 703-705, found by OCR search of the archive.org scan
items.summary: The ciphertext was transcribed from the images and aligned with the printed decipherment, rebuilding a mixed nomenclator. The rebuilt key read or corrected about 17 of the ~25 groups the print left blank, and showed that the dead king is Manuel I of Portugal, not the print's "Rey de Inglaterra".

items.title: John Armstrong to James Madison, coded postscript
items.primary: Library of Congress, Madison Papers, reel 10 frame 0521
items.secondary: Tomokiyo, cryptiana unsolved list; Founders Online (postscript undeciphered)
items.found: A State Department clerk's pencil decodes over Armstrong's 1806-07 despatches (NARA microfilm M34, roll 13), merged with Tomokiyo's partial table from a known-plaintext letter
items.summary: A 580-group code table (the "THE = 972" code) was rebuilt from the clerk's decodes in another archive, with the remaining groups inferred from their alphabetical slot. It reads 48 of the postscript's 49 groups; the 49th is a probable slip for "man".

items.title: Giuliano Caprile and Alfonso Cistarelli (Eger, Buda) to the Este
items.primary: Archivio di Stato di Modena, Ambasciatori, Ungheria b. 4
items.found: W. Somogyi's printed decipherments of two letters, Scriptorium VI (2025)
items.summary: Somogyi's two plaintexts were used as a crib to rebuild the 1520-21 homophonic sign cipher by EM alignment. The key then read in part two letters with no decipherment anywhere (R1139, R1136): the custode and governor of Eger, the late bishop's money.

items.title: Feuquières to Catinat
items.primary: Service historique de la Défense (dépôt de la guerre); printed in Mémoires et correspondance du maréchal de Catinat (1819), t. II pp. 283-284
items.found: Another letter in the same code, Louvois to d'Herleville of 6 Sept 1690, printed with its contemporary translation in the same Mémoires, t. I pp. 140-142
items.summary: The 418-group two-part "petit chiffre" of the Pignerol governors was rebuilt by aligning the Louvois letter with its translation and carrying the 72 shared groups over. 586 of 601 tokens read: Feuquières sets out the surprise of Veillane (Avigliana).

items.title: Fra Giovanni di Lucca to Ferdinand III
items.primary: ÖStA HHStA, Staatskanzlei Interiora, Chiffrenschlüssel Kt. 20 Fasc. 27 ff. 18-19
items.secondary: DECODE R2159; Tomokiyo, cryptiana unsolved list
items.found: Tomokiyo's published partial decipherment of the opening, "Al principe di trenti..." (cryptiana variable2.htm)
items.summary: Eight crib letters fixed from Tomokiyo's opening seeded an annealer that found a 24-figure Italian alphabet (all seeds agreeing, shuffled controls failing). Read in full: Grand Hetman Koniecpolski offers to keep the Turk off Rákóczi and supply 2,000 Cossacks.

items.title: Hugo de Moncada to Charles V
items.primary: Biblioteca Nacional de España, MSS/20213/12
items.found: The decipherment printed in Colección de documentos inéditos XXIV (1854), pp. 417-419, to which a pencil note on the leaf points
items.summary: 442 cipher signs were transcribed and aligned with the print by EM, rebuilding a homophonic key with code groups. The key reads the print's gap: Bourbon asked to be carried to Spain in the galleys.

items.title: The Venetian ambassador at Rome to the Doge and Senate
items.primary: Archivio di Stato di Venezia, IT ASVe 0045 010, Busta 27 f. 354
items.found: The contemporary decipherment of a different despatch in the same cipher, Mocenigo from Madrid (Busta 30, DECODE R1874)
items.summary: R1874's decipherment (~4,800 letters) was aligned with its cipher by EM to give a syllabary grid, which reads this Rome despatch unchanged. 1,280 groups transcribed; 99.1% have a value. Cardinal Barberini asks whether Palmanova is fortified and the Pontebba pass secured.

items.title: Alchemical cipher note on a flyleaf (Speculum volume)
items.primary: Zentralbibliothek Zürich, SCH R 201
items.found: Anne-Simone Rous's partial reading, published in U. M. Korn, Bilderfahrzeug (2023), p. 178 n. 41
items.summary: Rous's partial reading was used as a crib and the substitution completed from the original image: PRIMA MATERIA, VOM WIDDER, OFFEN. All 79 signs assigned; 78 coherent without correction.

items.title: Burghley to Walsingham, letter-book copy
items.primary: British Library, Harley MS 260 f. 419
items.found: A French letter in Walsingham's file asking for a ship to be kept waiting at St Valery (BL Cotton Vespasian F VI), identified from the BL catalogue
items.summary: A six-sign place name that recurs in four letters printed undeciphered in Digges's Compleat Ambassador (1655) reads VALERY. Only this place name is read (6 of 26 cipher tokens); the rest waits on a key not online.

items.title: Sir Francis Walsingham to Edward Wotton, ambassador in Scotland
items.primary: British Library, Add MS 32657 ff. 125-195
items.found: The bracketed glosses in the Calendar of State Papers, Scotland viii (1914), nos. 40, 41, 65, 106
items.summary: Signed letters in clear English with a two-digit name code; the calendar's glosses fix 19 Arran, 39 Gray, 40 Justice Clerk, 24 Farnihurst and 20 Morton. Two uncalendared letters transcribed here. About fourteen sign-alphabet words on 10 Sept remain open.

items.title: Bordeaux to Brienne (Thurloe intercept)
items.primary: British Library, Add MS 4200 ff. 88-90
items.secondary: DECODE R8390 (duplicates R8391, R8393); Tomokiyo, cryptiana (louisxiv0.htm)
items.found: The English Deciphering Branch's key sheet "To Mr. Bordeaux French M.r at London 1653" in a separate key volume, BL Add MS 32263 f. 1 (DECODE R7537)
items.summary: After a ciphertext-only solver failed on a faulty transcription, the key sheet was found and fitted: alphabetical syllabaries in three marked series. With 21 transcription corrections the despatch reads: the Council hears the Bordeaux (Ormée) deputies before Cromwell receives the envoy.

items.title: Johan Isaac de Swart (St Petersburg) to Pieter van Bleiswijk
items.primary: Nationaal Archief, 3.01.25 (Van Bleiswijk) inv. 610
items.found: Croiset's 1765 codebook for the Russia legation, a separate key record (DECODE R1038)
items.summary: The 1765 codebook, parsed to 5,961 entries, was found to fit and read 84% as transcribed; 34 values from context and 41 entries read from the key scans raised it to 96.7% of 1,719 groups. The French and Spanish answers to the Austro-Russian mediation, Catherine II's Greek project.

items.title: Dr Nicholas Wotton (Soissons) to Queen Mary I
items.primary: British Library, Harley MS 1582 ff. 8-10
items.secondary: DECODE R8499 ("N. Wottoy ? to unknown recipient")
items.found: A key filed in another archive and series, not tied to the letter: TNA SP 106/2 f. 162, "France 1554" (DECODE R354)
items.summary: The key (homophonic sign alphabet, nulls, ~140-entry nomenclator) was matched to the letter and corrected over eight passes: 75% of 2,801 signs firm, 89% with tentative values. Carew and the rebels at Compiègne with the French king and the Constable.

items.title: Robert Reade (Paris) to his cousin [Thomas Windebank?]
items.primary: British Library, Harley MS 7001 ff. 148-149
items.found: The Deciphering Branch reconstruction of the Windebank family cipher, in another volume, BL Add MS 32256 f. 4 (DECODE R9115)
items.summary: The Windebank key was found to read the letter; 11 values were rebuilt here. 94% read: Windebank's return under a summons, St Ravy and Mr Forster. The writer is identified from signature and endorsement as Windebank's nephew and secretary.

items.title: A correspondent at Randan to Louis de Gonzague, duc de Nevers
items.primary: BnF, français 3975 ff. 28, 30
items.found: Key no. 11 of the Nevers key book, BnF français 3995 f. 23, not tied to these letters by DECODE, the BnF or Tomokiyo
items.summary: The key book entry fits unchanged once the writer's glyph forms were learnt from a glossed sibling letter (BnF fr. 3413 f. 102). 26 of 27 cipher units read: Épernon passing near Lyon; the first letter is dated in cipher "De Randan", not Rome.

items.title: Prince Frederick of Orange (London) to the Hereditary Prince
items.primary: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague, Koning Willem I inv. XVIII-3
items.found: The 6x6 digit-square key recovered ciphertext-only in this project for a letter in another fonds, Prins Willem V inv. 339 (DECODE R1892)
items.summary: The R1892 key reads this letter unchanged; the clear Dutch under page 1 confirms it and fixes twelve word signs. Pages 3-4: scattered émigré troops, the Basel ratification, ambassadors to Paris. About twenty word signs open.

items.title: Charles I to Prince Rupert
items.primary: British Library, Add MS 18983 f. 14
items.secondary: DECODE R4921 (Non-decrypted; no decipherment in print)
items.found: George Lasry's reconstruction of the King-Queen cipher from other letters, TNA SP 106/10 (DECODE R929)
items.summary: Lasry's key reads the holograph unchanged: the King cannot convoy his artillery train and asks Rupert to march and fetch it. Groups beyond the key read from context; about fifteen code groups open.

items.title: Lope de Soria to Charles V: the key-B letters
items.primary: Real Academia de la Historia, Colección Salazar y Castro A-28 (9/28)
items.found: The court's decipherment of another Soria letter (30 Dec 1523) in a different volume of the same collection, Salazar A-30 (DECODE R9844)
items.why: same collection and correspondent, different volume
items.summary: Key B was rebuilt by aligning R9844 with its decipherment; the key-B letters read in substance (Siena, Beaurain, money for Swiss to descend on France, Andrea Doria). The earlier key-A letters were broken ciphertext-only and are listed in section 1.

items.title: Duke of Sessa to Charles V
items.primary: Real Academia de la Historia, Colección Salazar y Castro A-27 (9/27)
items.found: The Sessa key this project rebuilt from the court's decipherments in another volume of the same collection (Salazar A-31); four of the letters are calendared in CSP Spain ii (1866)
items.why: same collection and correspondent, different volume
items.summary: The key was recognised by recurring code groups and applied unchanged. Mostly already in print; the two uncalendared despatches (R9660, R9665) read in part.

items.title: London to Johann Georg von Ilten
items.primary: GWLB Hannover, Ms XXIII 1234:29,2 pp. 73-75, 119-121
items.secondary: Catalogue search of the Ilten papers
items.found: The "Chiffre-Tabelle" in another volume of the same papers, Ms XXIII 1234:31,1 pp. 386-391 (1745/46)
items.summary: The code table was matched to the letters through the worksheet values of one of them and reads both: 220 of 223 groups. The King approves the forage instructions so the French find none; an extract of Lord Stair's instructions.

items.title: András Bay to Ferenc Rákóczi II
items.primary: MNL OL, G15 Caps. D. Fasc. 81. 5
items.found: Rákóczi's syllabic key, G15 Caps. C. Fasc. 43. 56 (DECODE R609), picked by scoring all 94 G15 key transcriptions against the letter
items.why: same fonds (G15), different capsa; no link recorded before
items.summary: The key reads the letter unchanged (97.6% as sense) after seven transcription corrections: Muscovite and Polish envoys at the Moldavian court, the Tsar suing Charles XII for peace.

items.title: Philippe Groffey (?) to Ferenc Rákóczi II (alias Pompeio Cesoni)
items.primary: MNL OL, G15 Caps. C. Fasc. 39 pp. 277-279
items.found: The key "De Monsieur de Bonac et Graffei", G15 Caps. C. Fasc. 44/08 (DECODE R639), found by scoring the G15 keys
items.why: same fonds (G15), different fascicle; no link recorded before
items.summary: The key identifies 1,020 of 1,108 groups (92.1%), validated on two interlined siblings; the catalogue's direction is reversed (Rákóczi is the recipient). Ráday's letters to Rehnskiöld, Polish liberty oppressed in favour of King Stanisław.

items.title: Letters to Ferenc Rákóczi II (Poland and Danzig)
items.primary: MNL OL, G15 Caps. C. Fasc. 39
items.secondary: DECODE R912, R922 (catalogued as Rákóczi to unknown recipient)
items.found: The same Bonac-Groffey key, G15 Caps. C. Fasc. 44/08 (DECODE R639)
items.summary: R912 and R922 keyed at 97.4% of 2,352 groups: Stanisław, Charles XII, the Tsar, Rehnskiöld. The other two letters of the group were read from their own clear copy and interlinear decipherment and are not counted here.

independent re-solution; Tomokiyo solved it in 2025 (cryptiana unsolved list)
